sentence: This project builds image reconstruction methods using deep learning to improve the quality of tau scans in Alzheimer's disease.
This project uses humanized microbiome mice to find which microbial gut compositions help immunotherapy work against glioblastoma, a malignant brain tumor.
This project builds a positron emission tomography imaging tool that noninvasively detects damage to the protective myelin coating on nerves.
This project tests how well portable chest radiography and tongue swab sampling can find tuberculosis in villages far from health centers.
This project develops ways to turn simple building blocks such as aldehydes, alkenes and alkynes into molecules relevant to medicine.
This project uses mathematical models to study the chronic effects of cardiac resynchronization therapy and pacing of the heart under ischemic conditions.
This project creates a center that builds combined physiological models of muscle, cartilage, tendon and intervertebral disc to study musculoskeletal diseases.
This project studies how a protein found from yeast to humans works in membrane fusion and in infection by viral and bacterial pathogens.
This project studies how chronic ethanol drinking changes the balance of excitatory and inhibitory signals in brain circuits of monkeys and mice.
This project applies ecological and evolutionary ideas to test whether cancer develops in three distinct phases, from normal tissue to malignant tumors.
This project studies how cancer-associated fibroblasts block immune responses in pancreatic cancer and tests an inhibitor to improve the response to immunotherapy.
This project studies how microplastics change the mechanics, signaling and barrier function of endothelial cells under physiological flow conditions.
This project tries to find out how the catalytic domain of one protein converts to a protein phosphatase and how it regulates signaling pathways.
This project builds a deep learning tool that automatically checks the position of central catheters on chest X-rays of children.
This project uses mathematical models to predict the risk of drug-induced arrhythmia and how patient demographics and comorbidities change that risk.
This project develops an ointment with nanoparticles that deliver nitric oxide to fight infection and help burn wounds heal.
This project tests an optical imaging system that helps surgeons tell sarcoma tumors from healthy tissue during surgery using fluorescent dyes.
This project builds a model of succinyl-CoA synthetase deficiency in adult mice to study how the deficiency affects the brain.
This project builds a predictive platform based on a fluorescent protein that finds sensors for small molecules such as metabolites, drugs and environmental chemicals.
This project studies how a gene expressed in smooth muscle cells may be linked to peripheral artery disease, a form of cardiovascular disease.
